appeal.letter:
Subject: Appeal Against Denial of Claim dce20b69-20f0-bd7e-50a5-dc6f6787c504 – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period  

Claim Details:  
Claim ID: dce20b69-20f0-bd7e-50a5-dc6f6787c504  
Patient ID: dce20b69-20f0-bd7e-98ef-7d74b7d74b77  
Patient Name: Selena Bennie Feil  
Date of Service: 2026-05-26  
Total Claim Amount: INR 81,055.88  
Encounter Class: Ambulatory (AMB)  
Diagnosis: Osteoporosis (diagnosed on 2026-05-26)  
Procedure: Alcohol Use Disorder Identification Test – Consumption (AUDIT‑C)  
Policy: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER) – Coverage effective from 2024-12-23  

Grounds for Appeal – The policy defines a Pre‑Existing Disease as any condition diagnosed or treated within 48 months prior to the first policy start date. Osteoporosis was first diagnosed on 2026‑05‑26, which is after the policy start date of 2024‑12‑23; therefore it does not meet the definition of a Pre‑Existing Disease and the waiting period does not apply [suraksha_silver_policy#5].  

Grounds for Appeal – Clause 4.2 specifies that the Pre‑Existing Disease waiting period applies only to conditions that satisfy the definition in Clause 2.2. Since the condition in question does not satisfy that definition, the waiting period is inapplicable and the claim should be covered under the standard benefits of the plan [suraksha_silver_policy#11].  

Clinical Necessity – The treating physician will attach the clinical notes confirming the diagnosis of osteoporosis on the date of service and documenting the medical necessity of the AUDIT‑C screening as part of the patient’s comprehensive management plan.  

Reference to Denial Standards – Under the insurer’s own claims procedure, the burden of proof for a Pre‑Existing Disease exclusion rests with the insurer, which must provide documentary evidence that the condition existed before the policy start date. No such evidence has been provided; therefore the insurer has not met this burden [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].  

Specific Request – In accordance with the right to appeal within 30 days of the denial, we request that the grievance cell reprocess this claim without the pre‑existing disease waiting period restriction and remit payment of INR 81,055.88 to the provider [claims_procedure_and_grievance#8].  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition, ailment, injury or disease that was diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.1 Right to Appeal
citations.quote:
## C4. Appeals and Grievances  
### C4.1 Right to Appeal
The insured, or the provider on the insured's behalf, may appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter. The appeal should identify the claim, the denial reason, the policy clauses relied upon and the supporting clinical evidence.
